fields.question: Does CROP optimize model parameters, individual answers or the system prompt?
fields.answer: It freezes model weights and iterates the system prompt offline. The model generates; task and length critics identify accuracy and redundancy problems; a meta-optimizer rewrites the prompt. Deployment uses the selected prompt for one generation. This is neither hard truncation nor RL weight updates.
fields.example: Example: Iteratively changing “explain every step” to “keep the combined calculation and remove repetition” is prompt optimization; cutting any reply after 50 tokens is not.

fields.question: Why threshold the length critic, and how are the two textual gradients combined?
fields.answer: Section 3.3 runs length criticism only when generation strictly exceeds the threshold. Eq. 3 concatenates task critique, newline and length critique per sample for the meta-optimizer, rather than averaging numeric losses. Gradually remove narrative redundancy while keeping required calculations.
fields.example: Example: Threshold 40 does not trigger at 40 tokens but does at 41. “Check unit conversion” and “remove the repeated intro” cannot be replaced by scalar 0.7.

fields.question: What does CROP add beyond accuracy-only prompt tuning, and are token savings lossless?
fields.answer: It adds length feedback and selection by output-token cost. Table 3 includes accuracy drops: Gemini2Flash on ObjectCounting goes 96.0%→94.8% while mean tokens go 101.2→19.6. Report both sides of the tradeoff, not universal losslessness.
fields.example: Example: At equal 0.9 accuracy a 50-token prompt can beat a 100-token one. If the short prompt is less accurate, do not report only length.

fields.question: How does local selection avoid test data or a final unevaluated prompt, and what do callbacks establish?
fields.answer: Selection requires fixed validation revision/IDs matching the frozen CoT length baseline, disjoint training IDs, and no train/test scoring for selection. Each round validates the current prompt before proposing the next, so the final unevaluated one cannot win. Deterministic model/critic fixtures verify gating, concatenation and selection, not real LLM improvement.
fields.example: Example: Measured A=0.8 and B=0.9; last proposal C has no validation. Return B, not newest C.
